answer.justification: The space posterior to the stomach is the lesser sac (omental bursa). To access this space from the greater sac, the surgeon must penetrate the lesser omentum. The gastrohepatic (hepatogastric) ligament is a component of the lesser omentum that connects the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach, forming the anterior boundary of the lesser sac. Cutting this ligament provides access to the space behind the stomach.
